overview: Bendix Fust is a rodian bounty hunter from Rodia, documented across Knights of the Old Republic. Rodian hunter active on Manaan during the Jedi Civil War, when KOTOR-era guild boards still answered to Hutt and Sith paymasters.
history:
Bendix Fust rose from Rodia to become a rodian bounty hunter whose name appears on guild boards from the Core to the Outer Rim. Bendix Fust ran Rodian clan contracts on Manaan's kolto lanes, hunting debtors and Sith deserters when the Old Republic's authority thinned around underwater cities. Bounty puck archives, Imperial warrant logs, and Hutt contract registries all document Bendix Fust as a contractor who shaped wars without wearing a uniform. Coverage spans all nine saga films, Clone Wars, Rebels, Mandalorian, Book of Boba Fett, Andor, KOTOR, KOTOR II, SWTOR, and Sith Empire-era mercenary markets.

Even before Bendix Fust's career, Rodia produced hunters, soldiers, and syndicate enforcers whose traditions fed the modern guild system. Manaan's neutral kolto trade produced hunter-enforcers for centuries—Bendix Fust is the best-documented Rodian operator of the Jedi Civil War period. Old Republic bounty charters and Sith Empire mercenary rolls show how rodian bounty hunter contractors were hired to bypass political treaties. Mandalorian foundling laws and Hutt kajidic codes both influenced how hunters like Bendix Fust negotiate payment and honor.

In the modern era, Bendix Fust competed on postings issued by the Empire, the Rebellion, the Hutt Cartel, and independent monarchs alike. Bendix Fust remained active through Imperial guild consolidation, Rebellion-era shadow postings, and New Republic amnesty debates—pucks archived on Nar Shaddaa, Ord Mantell, and Nevarro alike. Post-Endor guild restructuring and New Republic amnesty debates still reference contracts linked to Bendix Fust. Mandalorian-era postings on Nevarro and Mos Espa show rodian bounty hunter specialists remain essential to galactic order—and chaos.

Bendix Fust operated in war zones where capture alive paid more than kill, and both paid more than failure. Fust clashed with Republic travelers and Sith patrols alike on Manaan, treating kolto convoys as hunting grounds for posted pucks and clan honor. KOTOR-era Nar Shaddaa boards and TOR-era Great Galactic War contracts show earlier generations of rodian bounty hunter hunters in the same blood-stained market. Jedi, Sith, and clone troopers alike learned to respect or fear Bendix Fust's approach to pursuit and extraction.

Imperial Security Bureau analysts note that hunters like Bendix Fust often know smuggler routes better than naval patrols.

Guild brokers classify Bendix Fust as a rodian bounty hunter whose name alone changes negotiation posture—feared on the Rim, cited in ISB redacted annexes.
